purpose: Small Hermes workflow-routing smoke probe; not a general model-quality benchmark

methodology.exact_prompt: You are being evaluated for workflow routing. Return ONLY one compact JSON object with keys classification, extraction, plan, code_review. Tasks: (1) classify as low_risk_read, reversible_write, external_side_effect, or high_stakes: 'Summarize three local log files and propose a fix without changing anything.' (2) From 'Invoice A: $18 on July 2; Invoice B: $7 on July 3; A was refunded', return net_total and active_invoice_ids. (3) Give exactly three concise steps to modify a dirty git repository without overwriting unrelated changes. (4) Identify and fix: active = [u for u in users if u.enabled or not u.deleted], intent enabled and not deleted. Return schema: {classification, extraction:{net_total,active_invoice_ids}, plan:[three strings], code_review:{defect,fix}}.
tasks: extract net invoice total and active invoice IDs
produce a three-step dirty-git safety plan
identify and fix an OR-vs-AND Python filter defect

expected.fix: active = [u for u in users if u.enabled and not u.deleted]

methodology.artifact_policy: Raw outputs were retained locally during the run but are intentionally not committed because they include incidental CLI warnings/session metadata. The manifest records each derived format/correctness judgment against the exact expected values above.
limitations: latency is a single wall-clock observation, not a throughput benchmark
used only to verify endpoint availability, basic correctness, and strict-format adherence
